newsitem.title: UK: Sterling off lows, seen well supported on dips.
newsitem.headline: Sterling off lows, seen well supported on dips.

text.p: Sterling recovered from earlier lows against the mark and dollar in afternoon Europe, helped by buying out of the U.S. and firm support below 2.74 marks and in the mid-$1.62-area, traders said.
Some support also came from UK January inflation numbers which came in a touch above forecasts.
"Even though the sterling movements look rather large, they are nothing extraordinary," said a trader at a German bank. "It's moving in rather clearly defined ranges now."
UK January retail prices were unchanged month/month but up 2.8 percent year/year against forecasts for 0.2 percent monthly drop and a 2.7 percent annual rise.

Ex-mortgages, inflation was up 3.1 percent year on year vs 3.0 percent forecast. "I wouldn't read too much into the figures, though they were slightly stronger than expectations," said Bank of Boston currency dealer Paul Crowhurst.

Analysts said while a rate hike is not expected before the government calls a general election, January inflation figures give a little more credence to the Bank of England's push for a small tightening in monetary policy.

"It is quite clear from Mr Clarke's (Chancellor Kenneth) comments that he is not going to raise interest rates ahead of the election. But in the run-up to the election, the markets are going to become a bit nervous," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
Traders said sterling's run against the mark on Wednesday was choppy as the currency tried to find its level after it scaled to fresh 52-month highs of 2.7685 marks on Wednesday.
"We are in the sort of areas that are very nervous for sterling. We are only a couple of pfennigs away from the pre-ERM breakout (2.7780 marks)," said Bank of Boston's Crowhurst.

In early dealings, sterling briefly slipped below 2.7400 marks but triggered few sell orders. Traders said bargain hunting at those levels then took it higher. A recovery in the dollar against the mark, after the greenback was slapped down in early dealings, also gave sterling a leg-up on the mark, said traders.
Overall, the pound's strong march against the mark is likely to continue, said dealers.
"The pound is strong, though not overvalued. It is still perceived as a 'safe-haven' currency and the market is banking on an eventual rate-rise," said a senior dealer at a UK bank.
